projects.name: Enterprise RAG Platform
projects.tagline: Document intelligence that answers with citations, not hallucinations.
projects.description: A retrieval-augmented generation platform that turns unstructured company documents into a queryable knowledge system. Hybrid search over Qdrant, semantic chunking tuned per document type, and grounded answers with inline source citations.

challenges.problem: Naive chunking destroyed answer quality on tables, contracts, and scanned PDFs.
challenges.solution: Built structure-aware chunking with per-document-type strategies and overlap tuning — groundedness jumped from ~60% to 92%.

challenges.problem: LLM latency made the product feel broken under real load.
challenges.solution: Token streaming end to end, retrieval-stage caching, and a re-ranking cutoff that cut p95 response time by more than half.

projects.outcome: Replaced hours of manual document lookup with sub-second grounded answers — adopted as the internal default for knowledge search.

projects.name: LLM Workflow Engine
projects.tagline: Multi-step AI pipelines with retries, fallbacks, and full observability.
projects.description: An orchestration layer for chained LLM operations — extraction, classification, generation — where every step is typed, retried on failure, falls back across model providers, and leaves a complete audit trail. Built because production AI fails in ways demos never show.

challenges.problem: A single provider outage took every dependent feature down with it.
challenges.solution: Provider-agnostic step contracts with automatic failover — outages became invisible; completion rate held at 99.9%.

challenges.problem: Debugging a failed 6-step chain from logs alone was guesswork.
challenges.solution: Persisted every step's input, output, and token cost as replayable state — failures now reproduce locally in seconds.

projects.outcome: Turned fragile prompt chains into dependable infrastructure other teams build features on without thinking about model failure.

projects.name: Realtime Ops Dashboard
projects.tagline: Live system state for the people who get paged when it breaks.
projects.description: A full stack monitoring surface for the AI platform: live pipeline health, retrieval quality drift, token spend, and latency percentiles — streamed to the browser over websockets and rendered without jank.

challenges.problem: Streaming 30+ signals froze the UI on mid-range laptops.
challenges.solution: Batched websocket frames, virtualized rendering, and canvas-based charts — steady 60fps at full load.

projects.outcome: Cut incident detection from 'a user told us' to under a minute — and made token spend visible before invoices did.

principles.title: Production is the only benchmark
principles.body: A system that works in a notebook has proven nothing. Real users, real load, real failure modes — that's where engineering starts.

principles.title: Latency is a feature
principles.body: Every AI product lives or dies on perceived speed. Streaming, caching, and honest loading states are product decisions, not optimizations.

principles.title: Boring architecture, interesting products
principles.body: Postgres over the exotic choice. Typed contracts over cleverness. Novelty budget goes into the product, not the plumbing.

principles.title: Failure is a first-class input
principles.body: Models time out, providers go down, retrieval misses. Systems I ship assume all of it and degrade gracefully instead of falling over.

currentFocus: Currently deep in agentic systems — tool-using LLM workflows with real guardrails — and pushing retrieval quality evals into CI.
